name: sobel3x3
description: A streaming 3x3 Sobel edge detector that computes Gx/Gy gradients with shifts/adds and outputs the saturated L1 edge magnitude |Gx|+|Gy|.
authorship: Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson

human_review.notes: Provenance (model and date) confirmed by the author; architecture, scope, and verification were directed and reviewed by the author.

spec.summary: Synthesizable streaming 3x3 Sobel edge detector. Pixels arrive in raster order on a valid/start-of-frame interface; two la_spram line buffers (depth IMGW) reconstruct the 3x3 sliding window. The constant +-1/+-2 Sobel kernels compute the Gx and Gy gradients using only shifts and adds (no multiplier), and the output is the saturated L1 edge magnitude |Gx|+|Gy|. The output is same-size (one output pixel per input pixel, zero-padded border) so frame geometry is preserved, and the streaming interface is shared with median3x3/conv2d so the filters cascade directly. Parameters DW (pixel width), IMGW/IMGH (frame size) set the data path width and line-buffer depth.
key_decisions: Streaming valid/start-of-frame pixel interface shared with median3x3 and conv2d so the three 3x3 filters cascade directly without glue.
Same-size output with zero-padded borders (one output pixel per input pixel) to preserve frame geometry across a filter chain.
Constant Sobel kernels folded to shifts and adds so the gradient path uses 0 DSP blocks.
Output is the saturated L1 edge magnitude |Gx|+|Gy| rather than the sqrt(Gx^2+Gy^2) L2 norm, avoiding multipliers and a square-root.
Two line buffers implemented with lambdalib la_spram (BRAM) at depth IMGW for the sliding window.
Self-checking testbench compares the RTL against a software Sobel reference.

origin.notes: Original implementation written for LogikBench; follows the cited algorithm/standard and hardware architectures, not copied from any specific HDL source.

references: I. Sobel, G. Feldman, 'A 3x3 isotropic gradient operator for image processing,' 1968.
R. Gonzalez, R. Woods, Digital Image Processing.
Standard line-buffer/sliding-window streaming filter architecture (e.g. FPGA image-processing line-buffer designs).
